guedy: guedy (gwedi) — after; preposition (A guedy y medwl hwnnw 'and after that thought')
daruot: daruot (darfod) — to finish, be finished, happen; verbal noun, with y/i of the person (kynn daruot idaw ymgueiraw 'before he had finished making ready')
y: y — (1) the article 'the' (y llys); (2) 'his, her, its' (y uryt: soft mutation = his; y hymdidan: h-prefix = her); (3) 'to' (y hela, y gyuoeth); (4) preverbal particle after a fronted adverb or object (yno y bu, Pwyll... a oed); (5) the relative in oblique relations (o'r a welsei) · (6) 'from' in y gan, y wrth 'from, compared with' (y gan y uarch 'from his horse'; y wrth y ffryt hi 'compared with her form'); (7) infixed object 'him, her, it' after a (a'y guelei 'who saw her'); (8) in a'y kymriw it is the second letter of ae 'either' (see a) · also (9) y am, y amdanaw 'from about, off' (y amdanaw 'off him'); y am hynny 'around that, beyond that, besides' · also (10) 'their' (for eu), with no mutation (y bot 'their being'; y kymryt 'their taking' = to take them) · also (11) 'in' (y'th wlat ti 'in your country') · (12) the particle y before mae introducing a reported fact (y may brawt … a wnaeth hynny 'that it is a brother who did that')
r: 'r — the article yr contracted after a vowel, apostrophe half of a'r, y'r, o'r etc.: 'the'
seithwyr: seithwyr (saith gŵr) — seven men, a company of seven; seith + gwyr (adaw seithwyr 'to leave seven men'); modern has saith gŵr
a: a — (1) preverbal/relative particle before a verb, causes soft mutation (Pwyll … a oed; ef a welei); (2) 'and' before a consonant, spirant mutation (a chanu, a fob); (3) 'with' (a'y gydymdeithon; gyt a thi); (4) vocative particle (A unben); (5) 'whoever, what' before a verb (a del 'whoever may come'; a wnaethost 'what you did') · (6) 3 sg. present of mynet 'goes' (nat a odyno 'that he does not go from there'; yd a hitheu 'she goes'); (7) interrogative particle before a verb (a oes …? 'is there …?'; a dywedy di …? 'will you tell …?'); (8) in a'y kymriw neu archolleu the editorial a'y stands for the conjunction ae 'either' (ae … neu 'either … or'; the Red Book has ae kymriw ae archolleu): read the two halves together as ae · (9) 'as' after an equative (kyn debycket a'r mab 'as like as the boy'; kyn ureisket oed a mab chweblwyd 'as stout as a boy of six') · also 'to, towards' with spirant mutation (parth a Hardlech 'towards Harlech'; y tu a Chernyw 'the side towards Cornwall')
dywedyssam: dywedut (dweud) — to say; 1 pl. preterite 'we said, we told' (a dywedyssam ni 'which we told of'); mutation after relative a not visible
ni: ni — (1) 1 pl. pronoun 'we/us' (yd ymdidanyssam ni); (2) negative particle, spelling variant of ny before some verbs (ni ladaf, ni bu)
uchot: uchod (uchod) — above, up there; adverb, spelt uchot (yn y perllan uchot 'in the orchard above')
penn: penn (pen) — head, end; noun m., base form (Penn Annwuyn 'Head of Annwfn')
bendigeiduran: Proper name — Bendigeidfran (Bendigeid 'blessed' + bran 'raven, crow'), son of Llŷr, king of the Island of the Mighty; bran is soft-mutated (b>u, u = f) as the second element of the compound; the name itself is unmutated as subject (Bendigeiduran uab Llyr a oed urenhin)
yn: yn — (1) 'in' (yn Arberth; nasal mutation: yn nyblyc); (2) predicative 'as' with soft mutation (yn wisc hela, yn arglwyd); (3) with a verbal noun, progressive (yn dyuot 'coming'); (4) before an adjective, adverbial (yn llawen 'gladly') · (5) yn yd 'to where' (ymchwelut yn yd oed Pwyll 'returning to where Pwyll was') · also yn yd 'as, while, when' (Ac yn yd aeth pawb ym pen yr arueu 'and while all went to arms'; the sense uncertain)
gwynuryn: Proper name — Gwynfryn (Gwynfryn), 'White Hill', the hill in London (gwyn 'white' + bryn 'hill', b>u/f inside the compound); radical (hyt y Gwynuryn 'as far as the White Hill')
llundein: Proper name — Llundein (Llundain), London; no mutation (ll- has no nasal form after yn 'in'; also after hyt 'as far as' and as object of kyrchwch)
wyneb: gwyneb (wyneb) — face; noun m., base unmutated form
ar: ar — (1) preposition 'on, upon; at' (ar Hafgan; ar y carw; ar y gilyd 'against the other'); (2) the article yr after a vowel, 'that which' (noc ar a uu 'than what was'; Ar ny del 'and whoever does not come') · also (3) 'with, accompanied by' (ar y ganuet marchauc 'with his hundred horsemen'); 'in' (ar y ssynnwyr e hun 'in his own senses'; ar perued y digrifwch 'in the middle of the merriment'); ar neill law Pwyll 'on one side of Pwyll'; ar uyrr 'quickly'; ar hynny 'thereupon' (see yny) · also 'over' (ar yr ynys hon 'over this island'); 'after the manner of' (ar ureint kyweirdeb 'in the manner of the arrangement'); 'on' a decision (disgynnu ar gymryt hynny 'settled on taking that'); 'ar ol' 'after' (ar ol Matholwch 'after Matholwch'); ar dec 'on ten' (see dec) · also 'concerning, about', where am would be expected (ac ar Yspydaut Benn 'and concerning the Hospitality of the Head'; the Red Book also ar)
freinc: Ffreinc (Ffrainc) — France, the Franks; proper name f., spelt Freinc (f for ff, as in ford); no mutation (ar Freinc 'towards France')
edrych: edrych (edrych) — to look; verbal noun (edrych ar y carw 'to look at the stag')
wnaeth: gwneuthur (gwneud) — to do, make; 3 sg. preterite 'he did', soft-mutated after a; auxiliary in 'verbal noun + a wnaeth' (dechreu ymdidan a wnaeth)
dref: tref (tref) — town, homestead, settlement; noun f., soft-mutated (t>d) after the feminine article y (ar y dref 'on the town')
ac: a — 'and' before a vowel (ac ef); also the preposition a 'with' before a vowel (ymgael ac ef 'meet with him', ymordiwes ac ef) · the manuscript also writes ac before some consonants (Ac wal, Ac val, ac racdaw) · also 'as' after an equative or kymeint (kymeint ac ynot ti 'as much as in you'; mor anwedus ac ar y wnaethoed 'as unseemly as what she had done')
gedymdeithon: kedymdeith (cydymaith) — companion; plural -on, soft-mutated after possessive y 'his' (a'y gedymdeithon 'and his companions') · also soft as the complement after a verb (A bydwch gedymdeithon chwitheu 'and be companions, you also')
dodi: dodi (dodi) — to put; verbal noun (dodi y deudroet yn y got 'to put his two feet in the bag'; dodi llef ar y gorn 'to give a blast on the horn')
ucheneit: ucheneit (ochenaid) — sigh, groan; noun f.; object of the verbal noun dodi, no mutation (vowel); the adjective follows softened (ucheneit uawr 'a great sigh')
uawr: mawr (mawr) — great, big; adjective (grauanc uawr 'a great claw'); soft-mutated (m>u) after a feminine noun · also predicative, soft-mutated directly after the verb (nyt oed uawr y weilgi 'the sea was not great')
chymryt: kymryt (cymryd) — to take, put on; verbal noun, spirant-mutated (k>ch) after a 'and' (a chymryt lloppaneu 'and putting on clouts')
diruawr: diruawr (dirfawr) — immense, vast, exceeding; adjective (diruawr llywenyd 'immense joy'); no mutation
alar: galar (galar) — grief, mourning; noun m.; g- lost by soft mutation after o 'of' (nac o alar 'nor of grief')
yndaw: yn (yn) + ef — conjugated preposition 'in him' (angheuawl dyrnawt yndaw ynteu; yssyd yndaw ef)
holl: holl (holl) — all, whole; adjective, precedes its noun causing soft mutation (yr holl gyuoeth 'the whole realm')
gyuoethawc: kyuoethawc (cyfoethog) — rich, wealthy, powerful; adjective, soft-mutated (c>g) after predicative yn (yn gyuoethawc 'rich')
guae: gwae (gwae) — woe; interjection, followed by the pronoun (guae ui 'woe is me'); no mutation
ui: ui (fi) — me; object pronoun after an imperative (dygwch ui odyma 'carry me from here') · also the softened pronoun 'I' after a verb (Ny allaf ui arnaf a dywedy di uyth 'I cannot bring myself to do what you say') and as the second, emphatic pronoun in mi ui 'I myself' (A mi ui a rodaf 'and I myself will give'); soft-mutated from mi · also after gwae 'woe' (guae ui 'woe is me')
heb: heb — (1) 'said' (heb ef 'said he'), a defective verb used only for tagging speech; (2) 'without' + verbal noun (heb hanbwyllaw 'without troubling') · (3) 'past, beside' in heb law (heb law yr orssed 'past the mound'); see hebdaw · also 'without' + noun (heb ohir 'without delay')
ef: ef (ef) — 'he, him'; independent 3 sg. m. pronoun
nyt: ny (nid) — negative particle 'not, it is not', spelling before a vowel or in emphasis (nyt teilygdawt)
oes: bot (bod) — to be; present 3 sg. existential 'there is' (Nit oes yndi nep)
neb: neb (neb) — anyone; pronoun, used with a positive sense in relative/superlative clauses (o'r a welsei neb 'that anyone had seen') · also 'anyone' under a negative = 'no one' (ny thykya y neb ymlit 'it avails no one to pursue') · also in y neb a 'the one who/to whom' (y neb a dylyer y kymryt y ganthaw 'the one from whom one ought to take it')
le: lle (lle) — place; noun m., soft-mutated after kyfryw 'such' (yn y kyfryw le a hwnn 'in such a place as this')
idaw: idaw (iddo) — to him; 3 sg. m. conjugated form of y 'to'
namyn: namyn (namyn) — except, but; conjunction (namyn ti 'but you')
mi: mi — 1 sg. independent/emphatic pronoun 'I' (mi a wnn 'I know')
arglwyd: arglwyd (arglwydd) — lord; noun m., term of address
pryderi: Pryderi (Pryderi) — proper name, the son of Pwyll and Rhiannon, named from pryder 'care'; no mutation
na: na — (1) negative particle in a subordinate clause, 'not' (na dywedy di); (2) 'neither/nor' in a series (na guas ystauell, na swydawc) · also negative imperative 'do not', with soft mutation (na ouyn di 'do not ask'; na yrrwch geu arnaf 'do not lay a lie on me'; na hawl ef 'do not claim him')
kyn: kyn (cyn) — before; with a verbal noun (kyn uy rodi 'before my being given') · also the equative particle 'as', softening the adjective (kyn debycket a'r mab 'as like as the boy') · also 'although', with the subjunctive (Kyn ny bwyf arglwydes 'though I am not a lady')
genhyt: gan — conjugated preposition 'with you' (2 sg.), a variant spelling of gennyt (a'r got honn genhyt 'and this bag with you')
hynny: hynny — 'that (thing)'; demonstrative pronoun, very frequent (a hynny 'and that')
dy: dy — 'your' (sg.); possessive pronoun, causes soft mutation (dy gerennyd 'your friendship') · also written for the affixed pronoun di 'you' after the presentative wely (Ac wely dy yna dy uab 'and there, behold, is your son')
geuynderw: keuynderw (cefnderw, cefnder) — cousin (male, first cousin); noun m.; soft-mutated (c>g) after the possessive y 'his' (uab y geuynderw 'the son of his cousin')
yssyd: bot (bod) — to be; relative present 'is, who/that is' (sydd) (Gwr yssyd gyuerbyn; pa amgen uedwl yssyd yndaw)
urenhin: brenhin (brenin) — king; noun m., soft-mutated (in apposition or as object): Hafgan urenhin, y deu urenhin · also soft as the predicate complement (a oed urenhin coronawc 'was a crowned king')
ynys: ynys (ynys) — island; noun f. (yr ynys hon 'this island'); no mutation
kedyrn: cadarn (cadarn) — strong, mighty; plural kedyrn (cedyrn) used as a noun, 'the mighty', in Ynys y Kedyrn 'the Island of the Mighty'; no mutation after the article
chyn: kyn (cyn) — although, though; spirant-mutated after a (a chyn nyt ymdialwyf 'and though I do not avenge myself') · also the equative particle cyn 'as', spirant-mutated after a 'and' (a chyn ureisket oed a mab chweblwyd 'and as stout as a boy of six') · also 'before' (a chyn penn y pedwyryd mis 'and before the end of the fourth month')
it: itt (iti) — to you; 2 sg. conjugated preposition, spelling variant with single t (achos it heuyt)
ny: ny (ni/nid) — negative particle 'not', base form before a consonant with soft mutation · also spirant mutation of c, p, t (ny chewch 'you will not get'; ny thygyawd 'it did not avail'); soft mutation of g (ny wybydei 'knew not')
buost: bot (bod) — to be; 2 sg. preterite 'you were' (ny buost gyn hygaret guas 'you were never so lovable a lad')
hawlwr: hawlwr (hawliwr) — a claimant; noun m., from hawl 'claim'
tir: tir (tir) — land, territory; noun m. (dylyedauc tir a dayar 'a lord of land and earth')
dayar: dayar (daear) — earth, land; noun f. (am dir a dayar 'about land and earth')
eiryoet: eiryoet (erioed) — ever; variant spelling of eiroet (o'r a welsei eiryoet 'of all he had ever seen')
trydyd: trydyd (trydydd) — third; ordinal (ar y trydyd 'at the third')
unben: unben (unben) — chieftain, lord; noun m., un 'one' + penn 'head'; vocative form of address · also 'the chieftain' as an ordinary noun (gan yr unben 'in the mind of the chieftain')
wyt: bot (bod) — to be; 2 sg. present 'you are' (pwy wyt ti 'who are you')
ie: ie — yes; particle of assent, taking up what was just said
kyt: kyt (cyd) — although; conjunction, takes the subjunctive (kyt bwyf i yno)
gwr: gwr (gŵr) — man; noun m. (y gwr a oed yn lle Arawn 'the man who was in Arawn's place')
hwnnw: hwnnw (hwnnw) — 'that' (m.); demonstrative (y dyd hwnnw 'that day') · also pronoun 'that one' (A hwnnw uu y trydyd dyn 'and that one was the third man'; yw hwnnw 'that is it')
yw: bot (bod) — to be; present 3 sg. copula 'is', used in equative sentences (Sef yw hwnnw, Hafgan)
genhyf: gan (gan) — with, conjugated 1 sg. 'with me' (eres genhyf 'strange with me'; ryued oed genhyf 'it was a wonder with me'); the gan 'with' of opinion; no mutation
i: i — (1) emphatic independent pronoun 'I/me', echoing a verb or conjugated preposition (rof i, arnaf i); (2) spelling of y 'to' before a vowel or l/w (i waret); (3) spelling of y 'his' before some words (i wisc hela 'his hunting-dress') · (4) after ohonawch, probably the 2 pl. echoing pronoun chwi with its ch run into the ending (ohonawch i 'of you')
guelet: gwelet (gweld) — to see; verbal noun, gu for gw (A guelet a wnaeth 'and he saw')
lle: lle (lle) — place; noun m., base unmutated form
uy: uy (fy) — my; possessive pronoun, triggers nasal mutation (uy anryded; uy nghyffes; uy gherennyd)
allaf: gallu (gallu) — to be able; 1 sg. present 'I can', with g lost by soft mutation after ny (Ny allaf ui … 'I cannot')
uot: bot (bod) — to be; verbal noun, soft-mutated after a (ef a eill uot yn ediuar gennyf) · also soft as the complement of a verb (a dylyei uot 'that ought to be')
llawen: llawen (llawen) — glad, gladly; adjective, base form (yn llawen)
un: un (un) — one; numeral/adjective (un dyrnaut 'one blow') · also 'same' (yn un ansawd 'in the same appearance'; yr un ford 'the same way') and the pronoun 'one (of them)' (Un a gyuodes 'one rose')
ty: ty (tŷ) — house; noun m. (yn y ty yd oed cassec 'in the house was a mare'); no mutation
ditheu: ditheu (dithau) — conjunctive form of ti 'you' (sg.), 'you for your part'
gynghor: kynghor (cyngor) — counsel, advice, will; noun m., soft-mutated after possessive y 'his' (wrth y gynghor ef 'by his counsel'; gan gynghor 'by the counsel of') · also soft as the object of a verb (mi a wnn gynghor da 'I know good counsel') · also soft after a preceding adjective (yn y kyuyng gynghor 'in the narrow counsel') and as object (ni a gymerwn gynghor 'we will take counsel')
arall: arall — other, another; adjective (yr erchwys arall 'the other pack') · also pronoun 'another (woman)' (heb arall 'said another')
reit: reit (rhaid) — need, necessity; noun m./f. (reit ymi 'need to me' = 'I need')
oed: bot (bod) — to be; 3 sg. imperfect 'was' (Pwyll... a oed yn arglwyd) · also oed 'appointed time, tryst', noun m., = oet (gwna oed a mi 'make an appointment with me')
im: im (i mi) — to me; conjugated preposition, contracted spelling (Meuyl im 'shame to me')
wrth: wrth (wrth) — to, towards, according to; preposition, base form (dywedut... wrthaw) · also 'at' (wrth y danned 'at the teeth'; wrth yr ascwrn 'at the bone') and 'because of' (wrth hynny 'for that reason')
pha: pa (pa) — what, which; interrogative, spirant-mutated after a 'and' (a pha wlat 'and what land')
cantref: cantref (cantref) — a 'hundred townships', the main administrative division of medieval Wales; noun m. (seith cantref Dyuet 'the seven cantrefs of Dyfed')
dyuet: Dyuet (Dyfed) — proper name, the region of south-west Wales
yr: yr — (1) the article 'the' before a vowel (yr erchwys); (2) 'for, for the sake of' preposition (yr Duw 'for God's sake', yr guaret gormes 'for removing the oppression') · (3) 'for all, however' before an equative-type noun and a clause (yr araued y kerdei y uarch 'for all the slowness with which his horse went'); (4) in yr meityn 'for a while (since)'; (5) the verbal particle y, yd, written yr before a vowel (yr ymordiwedei a hi 'that he would overtake her') · also (6) the perfective particle ry written yr, softening the verb (yr gyscwys 'has slept'); the article before an independent possessive (yr eidunt 'theirs'); 'for' with an abstract noun (yr bychanet 'for the smallness') · also the article before hwnn, honn, 'the one' (yr hwnn y tu a Chernyw 'the one on the side towards Cornwall'; yr honn a uu tryded anuat paluawt 'the one that was the third unfortunate blow') · also yr (er) 'for all' before the relative a (yr a welsynt o ouut 'for all the grief they had seen')
edewit: edewit (addewid) — promise; noun (dy edewit 'your promise') · also impersonal preterite of adaw 'to leave': 'was left' (yd edewit y gwyr hynny 'those men were left')
riannon: Riannon (Rhiannon) — proper name, daughter of Heueyd Hen
mam: mam (mam) — mother; noun f. (a mam y mab, Riannon 'and the boy's mother, Rhiannon'); no mutation
yno: yno (yno) — there; adverb (ac yno y bu y nos honno)
rodaf: rodi (rhoi) — to give, put; 1 sg. present/future 'I will give/put' (mi a'th rodaf di)
medyant: medyant (meddiant) — possession, power; noun m., base form (y'm medyant i 'in my possession')
genthi: gan — conjugated preposition 'from her' (3 sg. f.) (genthi hi 'from her') · also 'with her' (kyscu genthi 'to sleep with her')
bei: bot (bod) — to be; 3 sg. imperfect subjunctive 'were, would be' (bei ar y gam 'if it were at its step' = at a walk)
itti: itt (iti) — to you; 2 sg. conjugated preposition (y 'to' + ti), spelt itti (itti y byd 'you shall have it')
o: o (o) — (1) 'of, from' preposition; (2) 'if' before a verb (o gwneuthum gam 'if I did wrong') · also 'on, by' (o pedestric 'on foot'), 'out of, from' (o'th garyat ti 'from love of you'), 'of' a kind (pryt … o uorwyn 'the looks of (any) maiden') · also agent after a verbal noun, 'by' (troi o Pwyll y got 'Pwyll turning the bag'); o gosp 'of punishment'
gyuoeth: kyuoeth (cyfoeth) — realm, dominion; noun m., soft-mutated after y/a 'his' (y gyuoeth 'his realm')
well: gwell (gwell) — better; comparative of da 'good', soft-mutated as the object of kyuarch (ny chyuarchaf i well it 'I do not greet you')
noc: no (na) — than; spelling before a vowel (noc a uu 'than what was')
wy: wynt (hwynt) — they; 3 pl. pronoun, spelling variant (heb wy 'said they')
kicua: Kicua (Cigfa) — proper name, the wife Pryderi chose, daughter of Gwyn Gohoyw; no mutation
uerch: merch (merch) — daughter, girl; noun f., softened after a woman's name (Riannon uerch Heueyd 'Rhiannon daughter of Hefeydd') · also soft after predicative yn (yn uerch y urenhin 'as daughter to the king')
gloyw: Gloyw (Gloyw) — proper name, grandfather of Cigfa, Gloyw Walltlydan 'Gloyw Broad-Hair'; also gloyw 'bright, shining'; no mutation
gwreic: gwreic (gwraig) — wife, woman; noun f., meaning as context decides (a'y wreic 'and his wife')
inheu: inheu (innau) — I/mine, for my part; conjunctive 1 sg. pronoun marking contrast (a'm kyuoeth inheu 'my realm, mine')
bo: bot (bod) — to be; 3 sg. present subjunctive 'may be' (Vrth ual y bo dy anryded 'according as your rank may be')
kyuoeth: kyuoeth (cyfoeth) — realm, dominion; noun m. (a oed yn arglwyd... o'y gyuoeth)
bit: bot (bod) — to be; 3 sg. imperative 'let there be, let it be' (A bit corn canu da 'and let there be a good horn for blowing'; bit hynny yn arwyd 'let that be the signal'); modern bydded
phei: pei (pe) — if; spirant-mutated after a 'and' (a phei); in a phei … pellaf … 'and the more … the farther' it works like modern po
aduyd: aduyd (no modern form) — perhaps; adverb (ac aduyd ys kymeraf gynghor 'and perhaps I will take counsel'); the Red Book writes atuyd; its make-up is uncertain
dalo: talu (talu) — to pay, repay; 3 sg. present subjunctive, soft-mutated after a (Duw a dalo itt 'may God repay you')
gydymdeithas: kydymdeithas (cydymdeithas) — fellowship; noun f., soft-mutated after dy (dy gydymdeithas 'your fellowship')
e: y — 'his', spelt e before a following consonant or in some spellings: e gwn 'his dogs', e weneb 'his face'; also the preposition 'to' in e uynet 'to go' · also 'her', with h- before a vowel (e hymlit hi 'to pursue her'); the verbal particle y (e deuthum i 'I came'); y of y wrth 'from' (e wrthaw 'from him'); and in e uynyd 'up', e ymdeith 'away' · also the article 'the' (E brenhin, E chwedyl 'the king', 'the news'); 'it' as dummy subject (E doeth im 'it came to me') · also the infixed object 'him' after a (pwy a'e lladei 'who killed him'; a'e guelei 'who saw him') and 'her' with spirant mutation (a'e chladu yno 'and burying her there'); and the y of y gan 'from' (E gan Uanawydan 'from Manawydan')
gedymdeithas: kedymdeithas (cydymdeithas) — fellowship, companionship; noun f., soft-mutated after y (kedymdeithas y ryngthunt 'fellowship between them')
oreu: goreu (gorau) — best; superlative of da 'good', softened after a feminine noun (y neges oreu 'the best errand') · also soft as predicate after bu (yn gystal ac y bu oreu 'as good as he was best')
allwyf: gallu (gallu) — to be able; 1 sg. present subjunctive 'I may be able' (tra allwyf kynnhal 'while I am able to maintain'), -wyf; soft-mutated (g>∅) after tra
byd: bot (bod) — to be; used two ways: 3 sg. future 'will be' (uyd elsewhere) and, with y-, the vivid present ual y byd 'as he is' · also 2 sg. imperative 'be!' (byd ditheu a'r got honn genhyt 'you be there with this bag')
os: os (os) — if; conjunction of a real condition (os hynny a uynny 'if that is what you want')
mynny: mynnu (mynnu) — to want, wish; 2 sg. present 'you wish' (y mynny di 'that you wish')
mynnaf: mynnu (mynnu) — to want, wish; 1 sg. present 'I want' (nys mynnaf 'I do not want him')
eneit: eneit (enaid) — soul; used in address as an endearment 'dear one, my soul' (a dos y eisted, eneit 'and go to sit, friend')
af: mynet (mynd) — to go; 1 sg. present/future 'I go, I will go' (a af 'will go')
gyt: kyt (cyd) — together; in y gyt (a) 'together (with)' (y gyt ac wynt 'together with them')
thi: ti (ti) — you; 2 sg. pronoun, spirant-mutated after a 'and, with' (gyt a thi 'together with you')
iawn: iawn — right, proper, correct; adjective/predicate (iawn yw gymryt 'it is right to receive') · also noun 'compensation, redress, amends' (dy iawn 'your compensation'; chael iawn 'getting redress')
ynteu: ynteu (yntau) — 'he, for his part'; conjunctive pronoun marking a change of speaker or actor (heb ynteu)
no: no (na) — than, comparative particle (no gyrru 'than driving'; no chyuedach)
hi: hi — 'she, her'; independent 3 sg. f. pronoun
amser: amser — time; noun m. (Amser a doeth udunt 'the time came to them')
bu: bot (bod) — to be; 3 sg. preterite 'was' (a uu 'was'; Llawen uu 'glad was')
hitheu: hitheu (hithau) — conjunctive form of hi 'she', 'she for her part'
dewred: dewred (dewrder) — valour, courage; noun m. (drwy y dewred ef 'through his valour')
wreic: gwreic (gwraig) — wife, woman; noun f., soft-mutated after a'y/possessive (ymdidan a'y wreic) · also soft after the article, as a feminine noun (y wreic 'the woman')
etwa: etwa (eto) — yet, still; adverb (nys mynnaf etwa 'I do not want him yet')
bydy: bot (bod) — to be; 2 sg. future 'you will be' (na bydy gyuoet ti a rei o wyr y wlat 'that you will not live as long as some of the men of the land'); no mutation after na
gerdassant: kerdet (cerdded) — to walk, travel, go; 3 pl. preterite in -assant 'they travelled' (Wynt a gerdassant trannoeth parth a Dyuet 'they travelled next day towards Dyfed'); soft-mutated (k>g) after the particle a
hyt: hyt (hyd) — as far as, until; preposition/conjunction (hyt ym penn y ulwydyn 'until the year's end'; hyt na bo 'so that there be not') · also ar hyt 'along' (ar hyt y prifford 'along the highway') · also 'as far as, so far as, as much as, to the extent that' with the subjunctive (hyt y mynnych 'as much as you wish'; hyt y gallwyf y gaffael 'as far as I can get it'); hyt oet y wled 'until the time of the feast' · also 'so that' with the indicative (hyt nat oed rym 'so that there was no use'); hyt yn Aberfraw 'as far as Aberffraw' · also the noun 'length, duration' after pa 'what' (Pa hyt bynnac y bydynt ar y ford 'however long they were on the road')
bynnac: bynnac (bynnag) — -ever, indefinite particle after peth/pwy etc.; 'Peth bynnac' 'whatever'
bydynt: bot (bod) — to be; 3 pl. habitual imperfect 'they were (being), they used to be', beside oedynt (ual y bydynt yn eisted 'as they were sitting')
ford: ford (ffordd) — road, way; noun f., f written for ff (y'r ford 'to the road'; yr un ford 'the same way')
wynt: wynt (hwynt) — they, them; 3 pl. pronoun (un lliw ac wynt 'the same colour as them') · also Wynt, Gwent, in the name Wynt Ys Coet 'Gwent Is Coed', a region of south-east Wales
doethant: dyuot (dod) — to come; 3 pl. preterite 'they came' (Y'r llys y doethant 'to the court they came')
gwled: gwled (gwledd) — feast, banquet; noun f. (gwled darparedic 'a prepared feast')
darparedic: darparedic (darparedig) — prepared, made ready; past participle in -edic of darparu 'prepare' (gwled darparedic 'a feast made ready')
udunt: y (i) + wynt — conjugated preposition 'to them' (Amser a doeth udunt e uynet e gyscu)
erbyn: erbyn (erbyn) — (1) against, by (a time) (erbyn hanner dyd 'by midday'); (2) 'to meet' (yn y erbyn 'to meet him')
dyuot: dyuot (dyfod) — to come; verbal noun (a dyuot y Lynn Cuch 'and coming to Glyn Cuch')
arberth: Arberth (Arberth) — proper name, Pwyll's chief court, modern Narberth in Dyfed
wedy: gwedy (gwedi) — after; preposition, spelt without g, as in modern wedi (wedy bwyta 'after the eating'); the loss of g is a variant spelling, there is no clear softening word
yna: yna (yna) — then; adverb (Yna y rodes Arawn y furuf)
dechreu: dechreu (dechrau) — to begin; verbal noun (dechreu dygyuor 'beginning to muster') · also the noun 'beginning' (ar dechreu kyuedach 'at the start of the carousing')
ymdidan: ymdidan (ymddiddan) — conversation, to converse; noun/verbal noun, base form (dechreu ymdidan a wnaeth ef)
uanawydan: Proper name — Manawydan; soft-mutated (m>u) as a person addressed, vocative (Kyuodwch, Uanawydan uab Llyr 'rise, Manawydan son of Llŷr') · also soft after at 'to' (at Uanawydan 'to Manawydan') and after e gan 'from' (E gan Uanawydan 'from Manawydan')
uryt: bryt (bryd) — mind, intent; noun m., soft-mutated after y 'his' (yn y uryt 'into his mind') · also ar uryt 'in the mind of', to the eye of, soft after ar (ar uryt y neb a'y guelei 'to the eye of anyone who saw it')
uedwl: medwl (meddwl) — mind, thought; noun m., soft-mutated after y 'his' (yn y uedwl) · also soft-mutated (m>u) after pa 'what' (pa uedwl yw yr eidunt 'what intention is theirs')
wrthi: wrth (wrth) + hi — conjugated preposition 'to/at her' (ny dywot ef wrthi hi)
welsei: gwelet (gweld) — to see; 3 sg. pluperfect 'had seen', soft-mutated after o'r a (o'r a welsei ef)
uydaf: bot (bod) — to be; 1 sg. present/future 'I will be' (byddaf), soft-mutated after a (mi a uydaf hebryngyat arnat)
pa: pa (pa) — what, which; interrogative adjective, triggers soft mutation of the following noun
arglwydes: arglwydes (arglwyddes) — lady; feminine of arglwyd, term of address
th: 'th — infixed/proclitic pronoun, apostrophe half of a'th, i'th, dy'th etc.: 'your' (possessive) or 'you' (object)
uab: mab (mab) — son; noun m., soft-mutated after a personal name in a patronymic (Guawl uab Clut 'Gwawl son of Clud') · also soft after predicative yn (yn uab y wr arall 'a son of another man'; yn uab y Pwyll 'a son of Pwyll') · also soft in apposition to a noun (uy nei, uab uy chwaer 'my nephew, son of my sister') and in address (Oy a uab Duw 'O son of God')
llyr: Proper name — Llŷr, father of Bendigeidfran, Manawydan and Branwen; radical, no mutation (after uab 'son': a patronymic leaves the father's name unmutated)
minheu: minheu (minnau) — I for my part; conjunctive 1 sg. pronoun, beside innheu (Minheu a baraf 'and I for my part will cause')
manawydan: Proper name — Manawydan, son of Llŷr, brother of Bendigeidfran; radical (subject, after a 'and')
rodi: rodi (rhoi) — to give, put; verbal noun, base form
mor: mor (mor) — so, how; adverbial intensifier, triggers soft mutation (mor lwydannus) · also môr 'sea' (hyt y mor 'as far as the sea'); noun m., no mutation
wled: gwled (gwledd) — feast, banquet; noun f., soft-mutated after the article y as a feminine noun (y wled 'the feast'; y wled honno 'that feast')
genti: gan (gan) — 'with her'; conjugated preposition, 3 sg. f., spelt genti (a chanawon genti 'and whelps with her'); no mutation
chwi: chwi (chi) — 'you' (pl.); pronoun (y'ch kynnal chwi 'to maintain you')
gwrogaeth: gwrogaeth (gwrogaeth) — homage; noun f., from gwr 'man', the formal submission a man makes to his lord
gaswallawn: Proper name — Caswallon (spelt Caswallawn), son of Beli; soft-mutated (c>g) as agent after a verbal noun with o 'by' (goresgyn o Gaswallawn) and as subject after the negated verb (Ny uynhei Gaswallawn y lad 'Caswallon would not wish to kill him')
beli: Proper name — Beli (Beli), father of Caswallon; radical after uab (patronymic)
yg: yn (yn) — in; preposition, spelt yg before a g: the g is the written trace of the nasal mutation (yg gwyd = yng ngwyd 'in the presence of'; yg got = yng nghod 'in a bag', with c>ngh after yn 'in') · also before k-: yg kylch y ty 'around the house' (yng nghylch), the g being the trace of the nasal mutation (c>ngh)
mae: bot (bod) — to be; irregular present 3 sg. 'is, there is' (y mae arnat o anryded) · also interrogative 'where is?' (Mae yr yniuer …? 'where is the company …?')
caswallawn: Proper name — Caswallon (spelt Caswallawn), son of Beli; radical, subject after the verbal noun dyuot (Dyuot Caswallawn am eu penn 'Caswallon came upon them') and before a verb
elly: gallu (gallu) — to be able; 2 sg. present, soft-mutated/g-dropped after a ('a hynny a elly yn haut' 'and that you can do easily')
treulaw: treulaw (treulio) — to spend, pass (time); verbal noun, base form
honn: hon (hon) — 'this' (f.); variant spelling of hon (no'r ulwydyn honn 'than this year')
arhos: arhos (aros) — to wait; verbal noun (Sewyll ac arhos 'stopping and waiting')
uo: bot (bod) — to be; 3 sg. present subjunctive 'may be', soft-mutated after phan 'when' (phan uo ef ar perued 'when he is in the middle of') · also soft-mutated after the relative a (llathen aryant a uo kyuref 'a rod of silver that may be as thick')
nes: nes (nes) — nearer; comparative of agos 'near' (nyt oed nes idi 'it was no nearer to her')
ninheu: ni (ni) — we, for our part; conjunctive 1 pl. pronoun (a gaussam ninheu)
wnaethant: gwneuthur (gwneud) — to do, make; 3 pl. preterite 'they did', soft-mutated after a (eisted a wnaethant)
hela: hela (hela) — to hunt; verbal noun (uynet y hela 'to go to hunt')
digriuwch: digrifwch (digrifwch) — amusement, pleasure; noun m., spelt with u for f (drwy digriuwch 'in pleasure')
wlat: gwlat (gwlad) — land, country; noun f., soft-mutated after the feminine article or possessive (y wlat; i'th wlat)
welsynt: gwelet (gweld) — to see; 3 pl. pluperfect 'they had seen' in -synt (na welsynt eiryoet 'that they had never seen'); soft-mutated (gw>w) after the negative na · also soft after the relative a (yr a welsynt o ouut 'all they had seen of grief')
nac: nac — (1) negative used in a direct answer, repeating the verb, 'no' (Nac attygaf 'I will not'); (2) 'nor' before a vowel (nac ymdidan) · also negative imperative 'do not' (nac arch dim 'do not ask anything')
kedymdeithas: kedymdeithas (cydymdeithas) — fellowship, companionship; noun f. (cadarnhau kedymdeithas y ryngthunt)
rydunt: y rwng (rhwng) — between; conjugated 3 pl. 'between them' (y bu duundeb y rydunt 'there was concord between them')
yll: yll (ill) — the pronoun used before a numeral, 'they (all)': y rydunt yll pymp 'between them, the five of them' (modern ill dau 'the two of them'); no mutation
pedwar: pedwar (pedwar) — four; numeral m.; no mutation (yn pedwar dryll 'into four pieces'; a predicative yn would soften it, not shown)
gilid: kilid (cilydd) — 'the other, fellow'; used in y gilid 'to the other', wrth y gilid 'towards the other'
dyd: dyd (dydd) — day; noun m. (y dyd 'the day'; dyd da 'good day')
nos: nos (nos) — night; noun f. (y nos honno 'that night')
ymysc: ymysc (ymysg) — among, amid; preposition; ymysc hynny 'meanwhile, amid that'
aeth: mynet (mynd) — to go; 3 sg. preterite 'went' (a'y vreic a aeth attaw 'and his wife went to him')
at: at — preposition 'to, towards' (at y cwn 'to the dogs')
ryt: ryt (rhyd) — ford; noun f. (ar y ryt 'at the ford')
lywenyd: llywenyd (llawenydd) — joy, gladness; noun m. (diruawr lywenyd 'huge gladness'); soft-mutated (ll>l) after the preceding adjective diruawr
uu: bot (bod) — to be; 3 sg. preterite 'was' (bu), soft-mutated after a (tirionwch... a uu y ryngthunt) · also soft-mutated after tra 'while' (tra uu da ganthunt 'while it was good with them') · also soft-mutated after yny 'until' (yny uu damunet gantunt 'until there was desire in them') and as after the relative a left unwritten (A hwnnw uu y trydyd dyn 'and that one was the third man')
diolwch: diolwch (diolch) — to thank; verbal noun/imperative-like (diolwch y'r gwr 'thank the man') · also noun 'thanks, gratitude' (diolwch ac elwissen 'thanks and alms-merit')
ymchwelut: ymchwelut (ymchwelyd) — to turn (oneself); verbal noun (ymchwelut e weneb at yr erchwyn)
kymryt: kymryt (cymryd) — to take, receive; verbal noun (iawn yw gymryt; kymryt gwrogaeth)
orugant: gwneuthur (gwneud) — to do, make; 3 pl. preterite 'they did' (a orugant), older form beside wnaethant
canys: canys — since, for, because; conjunction (canys dechreueist uy llad 'since you have begun to kill me')
prif: prif (prif) — chief, main; adjective (prif lys idaw 'his chief court')
lys: llys (llys) — court; noun f., soft-mutated after possessive y 'his' (parth a'y lys) · also soft after prif 'chief', which softens the noun it precedes (prif lys 'chief court')
pob: pob (pob) — each, every; adjective (pob un 'each one')
anryded: anryded (anrhydedd) — rank, standing; noun m./f. ('o anryded' 'of rank')
bwyta: bwyta (bwyta) — to eat; verbal noun, also 'eating, a meal' (gwedy y bwyta kyntaf 'after the first eating', the first sitting of a feast)
kyntaf: kyntaf (cyntaf) — first; superlative of kynt, used adverbially and adjectivally
tra: tra (tra) — while; conjunction (tra deweis wrthyt ti 'while I kept silent') · also (2) 'very', before an adjective with spirant mutation (tra chyuoethauc 'very mighty'); (3) 'while' with the verb sometimes soft-mutated (tra barhaud)
uei: bot (bod) — to be; 3 sg. imperfect subjunctive 'might be', soft-mutated after a (a uei uwy no hynny) · also soft-mutated after ban 'when' (ban uei uwyaf 'when it was most')
kyuodi: kyuodi (cyfodi) — to rise, get up; verbal noun (kyuodi a oruc 'he rose')
allan: allan — out, forth; adverb ('o hynny allan' 'from then on')
chyrchu: kyrchu (cyrchu) — to make for, head towards; verbal noun, spirant-mutated after a (a chyrchu y bordeu 'and making for the tables')
gorssed: gorssed (gorsedd) — mound (one a lord might sit on), seat; noun f. (penn gorssed 'the top of a mound'; Gorssed Arberth 'the Mound of Arberth')
yniuer: niuer (nifer) — company, host; noun m. with prosthetic y- (yr yniuer y buam doe 'the company that we were yesterday')
ual: ual (fel) — as, like; conjunction/preposition (ual hynn 'like this') · also 'so that' (ual yd ymglywynt 'so that they could hear one another'; ual y bydynt gadarnach 'so that they would be stronger') and 'how' (sef ual yd eistedyssant 'that is how they sat')
bydant: bot (bod) — to be; 3 pl. present (habitual) 'they are', a vivid present in past narrative (Val y bydant y kerdet 'as they were walking'; the Red Book has the same); radical after the particle y
eisted: eisted (eistedd) — to sit; verbal noun (eisted a wnaethant 'they sat')
yuelly: yuelly (felly) — thus, so, in that way; adverb, the particle y fused with uelly (a chyt kerych di uot yuelly 'though you wish it to be so'; Ac yuelly y gwnaethpwyt 'and so it was done'); no mutation
llyma: llyma (dyma) — behold, here is; presentative particle throwing a scene before the reader (llyma yr erchwys)
chan: can (can) — since, because; conjunction, spirant-mutated (k > ch) after a 'and' (A chan derw yt 'and since it has befallen you') · also the preposition can 'with, by' (= gan), spirant-mutated after a 'and' (a chan hynn o wyrda 'and with these noblemen'; a chan pawb 'and by everyone')
ueint: maint (maint) — size; noun m. (a'e ueint 'and his size'); soft-mutated (m>u) after the possessive e 'his'
twrwf: twrf (twrf) — noise, din, tumult; noun m., spelt twrwf (ef a glywei twrwf mawr 'he heard a great noise'); no mutation (object)
ohonunt: o (o) + wynt — 'of them, from them'; conjugated preposition, 3 pl. (kyscu a wnaeth pawb ohonunt 'every one of them slept'); no mutation
ol: ol (ôl) — track, trace; noun m. (yn ol y cwn 'after the hounds'; yn y ol 'in its track')
phan: pan (pan) — when; spirant-mutated after a 'and' (A phan doeth yno) · also spirant-mutated after no 'than' (no phan uuassei 'than when he had been')
welynt: gwelet (gweld) — to see; 3 pl. imperfect 'they saw', soft-mutated after a (wynt a welynt 'they saw'; yny welynt 'until they saw')
ryw: ryw (rhyw) — some, some kind of; before its noun (ryw ystyr hut 'some meaning of magic') · also y ryw wr 'what kind of man'; ryw 'sort, kind' as a noun
dim: dim — anything, nothing; indefinite pronoun (ny russya dim ragot 'nothing will obstruct before you')
dyn: dyn (dyn) — man, person; noun m. (y dyn eithaf 'the farthest man')
eithyr: eithyr (eithr) — except; conjunction/preposition (eithyr gadu 'except to leave')
tei: tei — obscure word after brethyn llwyt 'grey cloth'; meaning uncertain, perhaps 'of the house, homespun'; editors have not settled it
llys: llys (llys) — court; noun f., base form
yndi: yn (yn) + hi — conjugated preposition 'in her/it', feminine (Nit oes yndi nep; y guassanaeth yndi)
hun: hun (hun) — self, own; also 'sleep' as a separate noun by context (e hunan/e hun 'himself'; kymryt hun 'to take sleep')
wybot: gwybot (gwybod) — knowledge, discernment; noun m. used substantively (ny bu gystal dy wybot 'your judgement was never so good') · also the verbal noun 'to know, find out', soft-mutated after y 'to' (y wybot pwy yw 'to find out who she is')
wrthunt: wrth (wrth) + wynt — 'to, at, towards them'; conjugated preposition, 3 pl. (a uu wrthunt 'there was to them'); no mutation
onyt: onyt (onid) — unless; conjunction (onyt ti a'm gwrthyt 'unless (it be) you (who) reject me')
hynn: hynn (hyn) — 'this'; demonstrative, substantive use in ual hynn 'like this, thus' · also adjective 'this' after its noun (seith cantref hynn 'these seven cantrefs')
awn: mynet (mynd) — to go; 1 pl. 'let us go' (Awn parth a'r llys 'let us go towards the court') or 'we will go' (ni a awn)
yneuad: neuad (neuadd) — hall; noun f., spelt with prothetic y- (Y'r yneuad yd aethont 'into the hall they went'); no mutation
nit: nyt (nid) — negative particle 'not, there is not', spelling before a vowel (Nit oes; Nit yttoydwn)
kyrchu: kyrchu (cyrchu) — to make for, head towards; verbal noun (Kyrchu y llys a oruc ynteu)
ystauell: ystauell (ystafell) — room, chamber; noun f. (na guas ystauell 'no chamber-servant')
diffeithwch: diffeithwch (diffeithwch) — wilderness, waste; noun m. (yn diffeithwch Iwerdon 'in the wilderness of Ireland'); the nasal mutation after yn (niffeithwch) is not written
honunt: o — conjugated preposition 'of/from them', truncated (o honunt 'of them')
ay: ay (ai) — is it?; interrogative particle (Ay uelly y mynny di 'is it so you wish?') · also ay … ay 'whether … or, either … or' (ay yma ay yn Ynys y Kedyrn 'whether here or in the Island of the Mighty') · also single ay 'whether' (e wybot ay gwir a dywedir 'to find out whether what is said is true')
darmerth: darmerth (darmerth) — preparation, provision; noun, paired with arlwy (y wled a'r arlwy a'r darmerth 'the feast and the banquet and the preparation')
kic: kic (cig) — meat, flesh; noun m. (-c = g); object of the verbal noun, no mutation
blwydyn: blwydyn (blwyddyn) — year; noun f. (hyt ym penn y ulwydyn 'until the year's end')
eil: eil (ail) — second; ordinal numeral (yr eil 'the second')
digrif: digrif (digri) — pleasant, amusing; adjective (y bu digrif ganthaw 'it was pleasant to him')
gantunt: gan (gan) — with; conjugated preposition 3 pl. 'with them' (a'r gennadwri honno gantunt 'with that message with them')
dioer: dioer — assuredly, indeed; an oath, a worn-down Duw a wyr 'God knows'
arnunt: ar — conjugated preposition 'on them' (Sef lliw oed arnunt 'this was the colour that was on them')
gwneuthur: gwneuthur (gwneud) — to do, make; verbal noun/infinitive, also used as the periphrastic auxiliary 'do' (a wneuthum itt 'that I did to you')
lliwaw: lliwaw (lliwio) — to colour; also to reproach, cast up against, taunt (yn lliwaw idaw hynny 'reproaching him with that'); verbal noun after yn, no mutation
gan: gan (gan) — with, by; preposition, softening the next word; possession is 'with' a person or thing (oed gan y march 'the horse had', literally 'was with the horse'); y gan 'from' (y gan y uarch 'from his horse'); base of gennyf, ganthaw, genthi etc. · also 'from', without y (ny chaffei namyn yr un atteb gan y gwraged 'she would get only the same answer from the women'; yny gigleu gan lawer 'until he heard from many')
llaes: llaes (llaes) — trailing, slack, loose; adjective, part of the epithet Llassar Llaes Gyfnewit; no mutation
llassar: Proper name — Llasar (Llassar), the giant in Llassar Llaes Gyfnewit, who came out of the Lake of the Cauldron; radical; llasar also means 'blue, azure'
racdaw: rac (rhag) + ef — conjugated preposition 'before him, on his way' (y kerdaud Arawn racdaw)
gelwir: galw (galw) — to call, name; impersonal present 'is called' (Ac y gelwir y rei hynny 'and those are called'), -ir, a>e by affection; no mutation after the particle y
am: am — preposition 'about, around; concerning' (am y uynwgyl 'about his neck'; am dir a dayar 'about land') · also 'for, in return for' (am y gam 'for his wrong'; am pob un 'for each one')
wneuthur: gwneuthur (gwneud) — to do, make; verbal noun (y wneuthur kynnadeu at Pwyll 'to send envoys to Pwyll', literally 'to make messengers'); soft-mutated (gw>w) after the preposition y 'to'
dros: dros (dros) — over, across; preposition (dros pedrein y uarch 'over the crupper of his horse')
yny: yny (hyd oni) — until; so that; conjunction, with a vivid present (yny hyllt, yny dyrr, yny uyd) or the subjunctive for a future goal (yny delych) · also in Ac ar yny llyma, a slip for ar hynny 'thereupon', kept as written (the Red Book has ar hynny) (Ac ar yny, llyma y teulu 'and thereupon, behold the warband')
ganthunt: gan — conjugated preposition 'with them' (ni bu newydach ganthunt 'it was no more novel to them')
hyny: hynny (hynny) — that; demonstrative pronoun, spelt hyny with one n, kept as written (the Red Book has hynny) (arnaw hyny 'on him, that')
lad: lladd (lladd) — to kill; verbal noun (am lad o honaf uu hun uy mab 'for my killing of my own son'); soft-mutated (ll>l) after the preposition am · also soft-mutated (ll>l) after the possessive 'e 'his' (na'e lad 'nor his killing')
gedymdeith: kedymdeith (cydymaith) — companion; noun m., soft-mutated as object (yn gedymdeith 'as a companion')
wynteu: wynt (hwynt) — they, for their part; conjunctive 3 pl. pronoun (Wynteu hagen ni wybuyssynt)
kynghor: kynghor (cyngor) — counsel, advice; noun m., base form (Kynghor yw hynny 'that is counsel'; gan gynghor 'by the counsel')
adaw: adaw (gadael) — to leave; verbal noun, a form without g- (A dyuot cof idaw adaw y drws yn agoret 'and he remembered leaving the door open'); no mutation
rof: rwng (rhwng) + i — conjugated preposition 'between me' (y rof i a Duw 'between me and God')
llad: llad (lladd) — to kill; verbal noun, base form (y'm llad i 'to kill me') · also llad glwm 'to tie a knot' (idiomatic, literally 'strike a knot'): llad glwm ar garryeu y got 'to tie a knot on the straps of the bag'
racco: racco (acw) — yonder; adverb after a noun (yr unbennes racco 'the lady yonder')
wyntwy: wynt (hwynt) — they, them; emphatic doubled 3 pl. pronoun wyntwy (hwyntwy) (kymereis wyntwy arnaf 'I took them on myself'); no mutation
drwc: drwc (drwg) — evil, harm, wrong; noun m. (ny chewch un drwc 'you will get no harm'); no mutation
uydei: bot (bod) — to be; 3 sg. habitual imperfect 'would be, used to be' (bydei), soft-mutated after a fronted word, the relative a being understood (pellaf uydei hitheu 'the farther she would be')
arnam: ar (ar) + ni — 'on us'; conjugated preposition, 1 pl. (drwc arnam 'harm on us'); no mutation
wneit: gwneuthur (gwneud) — to do, make; impersonal imperfect 'was being done' (o'r bedyd a wneit yna 'with the baptism that was then done'), -it; soft-mutated (gw>w) after the relative a
ys: ys (ys) — 'it is'; copula particle introducing a predicate, esp. in time expressions (ys blwydyn 'it is a year' = for a year) · also the infixed 3 sg. object 's 'it' after pei (pei ys guelwn 'if I saw it') · also 'below, under', is, in the name Wynt Ys Coet 'Gwent Is Coed' · also before the verb in ac aduyd ys kymeraf 'and perhaps I will take' (the Red Book atuyd ys kymeraf): perhaps the particle, perhaps the infixed 's 'it' after aduyd; uncertain
guell: guell (gwell) — better; comparative adjective, in kyuarch guell 'greet' (literally 'ask better')
gymerwn: kymryt (cymryd) — to take; 1 pl. present/future 'we take, we will take' (-wn) (a chynghor a gymerwn); soft-mutated (k>g) after the particle a
wdom: gwybot (gwybod) — to know; 1 pl. present 'we know' (ni a wdom 'we know'); soft-mutated (g>∅) after the particle a
da: da — good; adjective, also 'goods, wealth' as a noun (treulaw dy da 'spending your wealth')
lliw: lliw (lliw) — colour; noun m., base unmutated form (Sef lliw oed arnunt)
dodyssynt: dodi (dodi) — to put, place; 3 pl. pluperfect 'they had put' (y lle y dodyssynt y mab 'the place where they had put the boy'), -yssynt; no mutation after the particle y
taryan: taryan (tarian) — shield; noun f. (dyrchauael taryan 'raising a shield', swch y taryan 'the point of the shield'); no mutation (radical, object of the verbal noun)
wneynt: gwneuthur (gwneud) — to do, make; 3 pl. imperfect 'they would do', soft-mutated after a (kyuarch guell a wneynt idaw)
buant: bot (bod) — to be; 3 pl. preterite 'they were' (Ny buant 'they were not')
doeth: dyuot (dod) — to come; 3 sg. preterite 'came' (a doeth 'and came')
bot: bot (bod) — to be; verbal noun (hyt na bo... uot 'so that there be...')
gwyr: gwr (gŵr) — men; noun pl. (kymryt gwrogaeth y gwyr 'taking the homage of the men') · also gwyr 3 sg. present of gwybot 'knows' (onys gwyr Branwen 'unless Branwen knows it')
dienydyaw: dienydyaw (dienyddio) — to put to death, execute; verbal noun (neu yn dienydyaw am y mab 'or our putting to death for the boy': yn = ein 'our'); no mutation
mynnu: mynnu (mynnu) — to wish, want; verbal noun (Mynnu ymgyuathrachu 'wanting to ally himself by marriage'); no mutation
diuetha: diuetha (difetha) — to destroy; verbal noun (arnei e hun diuetha y mab 'against her that she herself destroyed the boy'; a'e diuetha 'and destroying him'); no mutation
lladwn: lladd (lladd) — to kill; 1 pl. imperative (-wn) 'let us kill' (Lladwn rei o'r canawon 'let us kill some of the whelps'); no mutation
glywei: clybot (clywed) — to hear; 3 sg. imperfect, soft-mutated after a (ef a glywei llef erchwys arall 'he heard the cry of another pack')
wyr: gwyr (gwŷr) — men; noun pl., soft-mutated after yn (yn wyr ymi 'as men to me') · also soft after o 'of' (o wyr 'of men') and in address (A wyr 'O men') · also soft after y 'to' (y wyr Dyuet 'to the men of Dyfed') and y 'his' (y wyr 'his men')
wnawn: gwneuthur (gwneud) — to do, make; 1 pl. present/future 'we shall make' (ni a wnawn yr oet 'we shall make the appointment'); soft-mutated (gw>w) after the particle a
yd: yd — preverbal particle used when the clause opens with an adverb rather than the subject, introducing an indicative main verb (A threigylgweith yd oed yn Arberth)
mynnych: mynnu (mynnu) — to want, wish; 2 sg. present subjunctive 'you may wish' (y mynnych ti 'that you may wish')
ymlad: ymlad (ymladd) — to fight; verbal noun (yn herwyd ymlad a frouedigaeth y gorff)
wnn: gwybot (gwybod) — to know; 1 sg. present 'I know', soft-mutated after a/ny, g dropped (mi a wnn; ny wnn i)
gwn: ci (ci) — dog; plural cwn, soft-mutated c > g after e 'his' (e gwn 'his dogs') · also gwybot (gwybod) 'to know'; 1 sg. present 'I know' (Gwn, Arglwyd 'I know, Lord'), radical form, repeating the verb of the question
barawt: parawt (parod) — ready; adjective, soft-mutated after predicative yn (yn barawt 'ready') · also soft after the feminine noun cad (cad barawt 'ready for battle')
ohonaw: o + ef — conjugated preposition 'of/by him' (edrych ohonaw ef 'his looking')
teccaf: tec (teg) — fair, pretty; superlative 'fairest' (yr ardurn teccaf a welsei neb)
gauas: caffael (cael) — to get, find, reach; 3 sg. preterite 'got', soft-mutated after a (a gauas 'got, reached')
amgen: amgen — other, different; adjective/adverb ('beth amgen' 'what else?'; 'amgen noc' 'other than')
goreu: goreu (gorau) — best; superlative of da 'good' (Goreu yw gennyf 'it is best with me' = I prefer)
pheri: peri (peri) — to cause, command; verbal noun, spirant-mutated (p>ph) after a 'and' (a pheri dodi gostec 'and having a proclamation made')
synnyaw: synnyaw (synio) — to heed, take note of, look after; verbal noun (a ercheis synnyaw wrthaw 'and bade (them) look after it'); no mutation
achaws: achaws (achos) — cause, reason; noun m. ('Pa achaws' 'what reason, why')
gelwit: galw (galw) — to call; 3 sg. impersonal imperfect 'he was called' (y gelwit Pwyll Penn Annwuyn)
tryded: trydyd (trydydd) — third; ordinal, feminine form tryded (trydedd) (A honno oed tryded prif rieni 'and she was the third chief ...'); no mutation (soft mutation after predicative yn is not written: yn tryded)
gantaw: gan (gan) — 'with him'; conjugated preposition, 3 sg. m., spelt gantaw (hyspys oed gantaw 'it was known to him'); no mutation
sef: sef (sef) — it is (this), that is; presentative particle introducing an explanation or answer
adnabot: adnabot (adnabod) — to know, recognise; verbal noun (adnabot meithryn yr ederyn 'recognising the nursing of the bird')
pallu: pallu (pallu) — to fail, give out; verbal noun (pallu y bedestric 'its speed failing')
guyr: gwr (gŵr) — man; plural guyr 'men' (gwŷr); gu- for gw-; no mutation (Y guyr hynny 'those men', after the article)
oll: oll (oll) — all, wholly; adverb/adjective intensifying a preceding noun (yr arueu oll 'all the armour')
bellach: bellach — any longer, henceforth; adverb (y'ch kynnal chwi bellach 'to maintain you any longer')
parth: parth (parth) — towards, side, direction; noun m./preposition (parth a'y lys 'towards his court')
